WOODWORK — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: WOODWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Run with the tool
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

2. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Input Cable Tester
   B. International Cricket Team
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. Information and Communication Technology

3. When learning Detailed drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Detailed drawing.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Detailed drawing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Detailed drawing.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Detailed drawing.

4. When learning Finishing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Finishing.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Finishing.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Finishing.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Finishing.

5. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   B. Ignore burnt cables
   C. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   D. Overload every socket

6. When learning Orthographic Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Orthographic Drawing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Orthographic Drawing.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic Drawing.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Orthographic Drawing.

7. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Monitor
   B. Keyboard
   C. Speaker
   D. CPU

8. When learning Woodworking Machines, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Woodworking Machines.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Woodworking Machines.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Woodworking Machines.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Woodworking Machines.

9. When learning Manufactured boards, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Manufactured boards.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Manufactured boards.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Manufactured boards.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Manufactured boards.

10. When learning Timber Defects, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Timber Defects.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timber Defects.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Timber Defects.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Timber Defects.

11. When learning Mass Production, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Mass Production.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Mass Production.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Mass Production.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Mass Production.

12. When learning Health and Safety in the Workshop, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Health and Safety in the Workshop.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Mass Production and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Finishing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Project activity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Orthographic Drawing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

2. D — Information and Communication Technology

3. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Detailed drawing.

4. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Finishing.

5. C — Never touch live wires with wet hands

6. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic Drawing.

7. D — CPU

8. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Woodworking Machines.

9. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Manufactured boards.

10. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timber Defects.

11. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Mass Production.

12. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and Safety in the Workshop.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Mass Production; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Finishing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Project activity; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Orthographic Drawing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
